source.title: Revisiting Glorot Initialization for Long-Range Linear Recurrences
source.authors: Noga Bar; Mariia Seleznova; Yotam Alexander; Gitta Kutyniok; Raja Giryes

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates whether Glorot initialization stays stable in long linear recurrent networks and reports instability with standard Glorot plus improved stability after a proposed rescaling. This refines the scope of initialization claims, though its primary measure is signal stability rather than classification training error.
record.gate_note: Reported results include spectral-radius and hidden-state measurements at initialization, plus downstream classification accuracies. The accuracy results are included as published, but they do not directly measure training classification error. The paper's comparisons to prior work in the related-work section are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures signal stability in linear recurrences and downstream task accuracy. It does not measure V4's learning speed or trainable feedforward depth, and its recurrent weight-sharing setting differs from the plain feedforward networks named there. None of V1–V6 is directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that standard Glorot can destabilize long linear recurrences and that dimension-aware rescaling mitigates this. They also report standard-Glorot training failures and the highest rescaled accuracy in four of six dense/diagonal task settings. Their hidden-state theory is a lower-bound analysis for complex Gaussian initialization with independent Gaussian inputs; optimization dynamics remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines repeated application of a Glorot-initialized recurrent matrix and proposes a dimension-dependent variance rescaling. It does not reproduce the feedforward training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on initialization (standard versus rescaled Glorot) and real versus complex matrix setting; the authors also distinguish fixed sequence length from the double-scaling long-sequence regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Real and complex Glorot recurrent matrices exhibit spectral-radius overshoot and exploding matrix-power and hidden-state norms; dimension-aware rescaling suppresses explosion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-width Glorot initialization can destabilize long shared-weight linear recurrences, while dimension-aware rescaling improves signal stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard Glorot models fail to train on all three sequence tasks; alternative initializations permit training and produce differing task accuracies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects trainability and downstream accuracy of linear recurrent models on long-sequence classification tasks.

record.problems: The theoretical hidden-state growth analysis focuses on complex Gaussian initialization and provides a lower bound under independent Gaussian inputs; the authors note temporally correlated inputs and exact characterization remain open. Numerical plots provide qualitative findings without tabulated values. The training experiments cover linear RNNs and report task accuracy, not training classification error. The supplied Table 1 is flattened, making some row-to-value assignments uncertain.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. The downstream accuracy table is flattened; only the values that can be associated with rows from the supplied layout are included, with attribution uncertainty noted.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and capacity or training-recipe comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with feedforward depth, identity shortcuts, deep tanh initialization, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable feedforward depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh training; 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning-rate thresholds, curvature changes, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the initial threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No version-level verdict follows from recurrent stability alone. Table 1's flattened layout can be reconstructed from its ordered rows; it does not support the record's claim that dense Rescale failed.

versions.untested_parts: Training from random initialization to near-zero classification error; CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training-error outcomes; corrupted or random labels; width and training-duration conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and effects of student width.
Plain versus residual feedforward networks, depth effects, special deep tanh initialization, and residual networks without normalization.

The paper tests the effect of Glorot and a rescaled Glorot initialization in linear recurrent networks, but does not test the activation-matched feedforward initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks named in this version.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss curvature, catapult behavior, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual training.

rows.subject: real Glorot-initialized matrices W ∈ R500×500
rows.operation_detail: Measured spectral-radius distributions over 100 independent matrix samples.
rows.measure: Empirical spectral-radius distribution; frequency of eigenvalue magnitudes exceeding one.
rows.value: Glorot often yields eigenvalues with magnitudes exceeding one.
rows.note: The paper states the qualitative result for real matrices; the plotted distribution is not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Spectral radius at initialization does not measure learning speed or trainable depth.

rows.operation_detail: Measured spectral-radius distributions over 100 independent matrix samples.
rows.measure: Empirical spectral-radius distribution; frequency of eigenvalue magnitudes exceeding one.

rows.value: The corrected initialization makes this much less likely.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; exact proportion is not stated.
rows.check: Reduced spectral radius does not establish V4's training effects.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: real and complex linear recurrent networks with long sequences
reader_labels.reason: Standard Glorot is reported to produce exploding matrix-power and hidden-state norms, while rescaling suppresses explosion but can cause slow decay; see R1–R12.
